title: Affinity Broker: Dedicated→Hosted Overflow Arbitration and Variant Degradation Profiles
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Problem: Tenant requests should prefer dedicated capacity when reserved, but capacity contention and transient regional degradation require safe arbitration to hosted endpoints without breaking tenant SLAs or causing quality regressions. Current heuristics are brittle: abrupt spillover causes token-cost spikes, higher latencies, and model variant mismatches.
summary_of_proposal: Introduce an Affinity Broker service that mediates Dedicated→Hosted arbitration with: (1) tenant-level grace credits and soft-reserve decay, (2) variant degradation profiles (controlled demotion of bigger models to quantized/cheaper variants with output-quality metadata), and (3) staged handshake with hosted backfills (capacity reservation negotiation and rate-limited spillover). The Broker exposes a decision trace for audit and observability.
tradeoffs: Complexity vs predictability: adding Broker increases routing surface area but centralizes policy and observability
Latency vs cost: staged variant demotions may increase token-efficiency but can add microseconds from policy lookup; we mitigate with cached decisions and local-sidestepping
Consistency vs availability: aggressive failback to hosted may temporarily change model outputs; we include quality tags and canary thresholds to limit regressions
technical_design_notes: Broker will run in the control plane and produce signed routing decisions consumed by edge proxies. Decision logic: capacity-aware scoring (free_gpus, queued_tokens, per-tenant reserved_ratio), tenant_priority adjustments, regional health penalty, and variant-score computed from model-perf profiles. Decisions cached at edge for up to 3s with a max-staleness metric. Variant demotion profiles are parameterized by: max_quality_drop_pct, max_cost_savings_pct, and degradation_window.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end flow: dedicated preferred when reserved and healthy; simulated loss of 50% of a region routes 95% of affected traffic to hosted with <=20% increase in p95 latency
Quality regression: synthetic prompts run through demoted variant must pass score thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity) agreed with Product for top-3 workloads
Cost guardrail: tenant-level cost increase when switching to hosted must be capped by tenant grace credits and automatic throttle
Observability: Decision traces appear in Console with route_reason, variant_profile, and decision_age; alerts fire on unexpected oscillation (>3 switches/minute)
Feature flags: end-user controlled feature flag in Console to disable Broker per-tenant
implementation_steps: 1) Design Broker API and decision schema; write protobufs and JSON trace spec
2) Implement scoring engine with unit tests + model perf adapter (offline profiles service)
3) Edge integration: add cached decision layer to routing proxy; build fallback handshake protocol
4) Variant profiles: add demotion recipes and quality validators into model catalog
5) E2E tests: chaos sim for partial region failure + load tests for caching behavior
6) Gradual rollout: internal dogfood, canary tenants, then broader opt-in
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal staging with 2 tenants, run synthetic failure drills and capture decision traces. Week 2: enable for 10% of production tenants with logs-only mode (no enforced routing). Week 3: enable soft-routing (edge honors Broker but with a 5s grace scoreboard), monitor oscillation and cost. Week 4: full-on for opt-in enterprise tenants. Immediate rollback: flip tenant-level flag to bypass Broker and revert proxy cache to last-known-good routing rule.
monitoring_queries: ALERT if rate(route_switches_total[1m]) > 3/min for any tenant
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for scoring logic; integration test suite that replays production routing traces with injected region failures; offline evaluation of demoted variants on canned prompt set; cost-sim tests to verify grace credit accounting. Performance target: Broker should add <2ms median to routing path when cached, <10ms cold-start policy evaluation.
open_risks: Model-quality regressions for subtle prompt classes not covered by canned evals
Edge cache staleness causing brief misrouting during fast regional recovery
Cross-tenant fairness: high-priority tenants could edge out medium tenants if scoring weights are miscalibrated
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Blake): ask to include customer-visible labeling in Console when demotion occurs
Design (Leila Ortiz): suggest small UX copy for tenant admins explaining grace credits and cost impact
Security (Ethan Cole): require audit log export and KMS signing for decision traces (added to security_review_required)
SRE (Anika Rao): recommend a circuit-softening timer to avoid flip-flopping under intermittent API errors
